players.note: Tykee Smith should continue his IDP dominance this season, and it starts in Week 1 against the Cincinnati Bengals. The Bengals offense should keep Curl busy all night, increasing the floor for one of the highest-upside plays of the week. Tap Tykee as a top-three DB option for Week 1.

The DB1 overall last season (settings dependent), Kam Curl is still not getting enough love from the fantasy community. Start him everywhere over everyone not named Tykee Smith or Kyle Hamilton, and the latter is almost a lock to be outscored by Curl this season. Fire Curl up with confidence as an LB1 play for Week 1 against San Francisco.

Quentin Lake is a DB1 play for Week 1. He proved he can maintain his IDP value in the slot last weekend and should see plenty of work against both the run and the pass against the San Francisco 49ers this week. Tap him as a top-10 option with serious top-five upside.

Kevin Byard is in the top-20 conversation for a plus matchup against the Seattle Seahawks. Byard should see plenty of work against both the pass and the run and should hit the ground running in a familiar scheme.
Julian Love is an easy top 24 option for a plus Week 1 matchup against Drake Maye and the New England Patriots. The secondary should see a lot of work in this one, giving Love a high floor.

Malik Mustapha makes for an excellent DB3 option who can double as a DB2 play depending on your roster depth. He will provide DB2 production this season, but most should have the luxury of deploying him as a DB3 or flex. Start him with confidence for Week 1, thanks to a plus matchup against San Francisco in Australia.

Kamren Kinchens is a solid DB3 play, but don't be shy about leaving him on benches for Week 1. He is at his best when he provides a big play, but has not been consistent enough to comfortably project him as a top-36 option with zero teams on bye. The decision will come down to your squad's roster depth.

Craig Woodson should remain on fantasy benches for Week 1. You did not draft him to start unless you play in 20+ team leagues, so keep him on the pine and evaluate his progress in what could be a breakout season for the young Patriots safety.
Christian Gonzalez should be left on benches in most formats. Those in INT-heavy leagues should take a look, but don't expect Gonzo to draw many targets in coverage when he is not covering JSN.

Ji'Ayir Brown is going to have his IDP moments this season but is not a suggested starter for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. His floor leaves him in bench purgatory while his upside places him in the upside DB4/flex2 conversation. You can do better in Week 1.
